conditions.name: Generalised anxiety disorder

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: Excessive, hard-to-control worry across many areas for six months or more, with restlessness, muscle tension, poor sleep and physical symptoms like palpitations.
workup: TFTs and ECG if physical symptoms prominent

exam.step: Inspect the tongue and mouth corners

exam.positive: Looks for a source of blood loss

labs.confirms: The single most useful test; low confirms
Mandatory in men and postmenopausal women

conditions.name: Iron deficiency anaemia

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Too little iron to make haemoglobin. Fatigue, breathlessness on exertion, pallor and sometimes odd cravings. In adults the real question is always where the blood is going.
workup: Faecal immunochemical test or endoscopy in men and post-menopausal women

exam.step: Observe during an attack if possible

conditions.name: Panic attack / panic disorder

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: A surge of intense fear peaking within minutes, with racing heart, breathlessness and tingling. Real and frightening, and a diagnosis of exclusion when cardiac risk exists.

exam.positive: Upbeating torsional nystagmus after a short latency, fatiguing on repetition
A normal head impulse with direction-changing nystagmus suggests central cause
Normal hearing distinguishes it from Meniere disease

labs.confirms: Therapeutic and confirmatory if symptoms resolve

conditions.name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: Displaced crystals in the inner ear. Brief violent spinning lasting under a minute, triggered every time by rolling over in bed or looking up. Hearing is normal.
workup: Reassess if hearing loss or neurological signs

exam.positive: Prodrome of nausea, warmth and tunnel vision
Normal; a murmur suggests structural disease

labs.confirms: Excludes long QT, Brugada, heart block

labs.test: No further test if history is typical and ECG normal

conditions.name: Vasovagal syncope

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: A reflex drop in heart rate and blood pressure, typically after standing a long time, pain, heat or the sight of blood. Warning nausea and greying vision come first.

exam.step: Lying and standing blood pressure at 1 and 3 minutes
exam.positive: A drop of 20 systolic or 10 diastolic confirms
Volume depletion is a common contributor

conditions.name: Orthostatic hypotension

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: Blood pressure falls on standing, so the brain is briefly underperfused. Common in older people, on blood pressure tablets, or when dehydrated.

exam.positive: Abnormal head impulse with unidirectional nystagmus supports a peripheral cause
Able to walk, though veering, unlike cerebellar stroke

labs.test: HINTS is more sensitive than early MRI for stroke

conditions.name: Vestibular neuritis

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Inflammation of the balance nerve after a viral illness. Constant severe spinning for days on end, not triggered by position, with vomiting and unsteadiness.

labs.test: FBC, CRP, ESR, TFTs, coeliac, B12, ferritin, glucose
Diagnosis after symptoms exceed three months

conditions.name: Chronic fatigue syndrome / ME

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: Disabling fatigue lasting over three months with post-exertional worsening, unrefreshing sleep and cognitive difficulty, after other causes have been excluded.
workup: FBC, CRP, TFTs, coeliac, B12, ferritin, glucose

exam.positive: Face, arm, speech deficit with a documented time of onset
Quantifies severity and supports the diagnosis
Hypoglycaemia is the commonest stroke mimic

labs.confirms: Distinguishes infarct from haemorrhage before thrombolysis
Detects atrial fibrillation as a source

labs.test: FBC, clotting, renal function, lipids, HbA1c

conditions.name: Ischaemic stroke

triage.label: Emergency
triage.action: Call emergency services or go to an emergency department now

conditions.summary: A blocked brain artery killing brain tissue. Sudden one-sided weakness, facial droop or speech failure. Treatment window is measured in hours, so time is brain.
workup: FAST assessment and note time of onset
Thrombolysis or thrombectomy if in window

exam.positive: Unsteady with eyes open too, unlike sensory ataxia

exam.step: Look for nystagmus and scanning speech

labs.confirms: Localises the lesion before any scan

labs.test: B12, TFTs, alcohol history and drug levels

conditions.name: Cerebellar ataxia
conditions.summary: Loss of coordination from cerebellar disease, giving a wide-based unsteady walk that does not improve with looking at the feet. Alcohol, stroke, tumour and drug toxicity are the causes worth finding quickly.
workup: Test finger-nose, heel-shin and rapid alternating movements
Romberg to separate cerebellar from sensory ataxia

exam.positive: A bruit suggests stenosis, though absence does not exclude

labs.confirms: Highest stroke risk is in the first days

conditions.name: Transient ischaemic attack

triage.label: Emergency
triage.action: Call emergency services or go to an emergency department now

conditions.summary: Stroke symptoms that resolve completely within 24 hours, usually within an hour. A warning shot: the risk of a full stroke is highest in the next 48 hours.

exam.positive: Sensorineural pattern on the affected side

conditions.name: Meniere's disease

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Recurrent attacks of vertigo lasting 20 minutes to several hours, each with fluctuating hearing loss, ringing and a feeling of fullness in the same ear.

exam.positive: A postural drop indicates significant loss
Spider naevi, ascites, caput medusae suggest varices

labs.confirms: A score of 0 may allow outpatient management

labs.test: FBC, urea, LFTs, INR, group and crossmatch
labs.confirms: A raised urea:creatinine ratio supports upper GI source

conditions.name: Upper gastrointestinal bleed

triage.label: Emergency
triage.action: Call emergency services or go to an emergency department now

conditions.summary: Bleeding above the small bowel, appearing as vomited blood or black tarry stools. Rapidly life-threatening; anticoagulants, NSAIDs and alcohol all raise the risk.
workup: Group and save, crossmatch, FBC, INR

redFlags.label: Possible sepsis
redFlags.message: A fever together with confusion, very fast breathing, mottled skin or a collapsing blood pressure can mean infection is affecting the whole body.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Do not wait to see whether it settles.

redFlags.label: Rash that does not fade under pressure
redFlags.message: Spots that stay visible when a glass is pressed on them, alongside feeling unwell, can be a sign of bacteria in the bloodstream.

redFlags.label: Possible severe allergic reaction
redFlags.message: Swelling of the throat or tongue with difficulty breathing after a food, sting, or medicine can close the airway within minutes.
redFlags.action: Use an adrenaline auto-injector if you have one, then call emergency services.

redFlags.label: Reduced consciousness
redFlags.message: Being difficult to rouse, or drifting in and out of awareness, always needs immediate assessment whatever the cause.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Place the person on their side if unresponsive.

redFlags.label: Blackout with exertion or palpitations
redFlags.message: Passing out during exercise, or alongside a racing heart or chest pain, can point to a dangerous heart rhythm rather than a simple faint.
redFlags.action: Seek same-day medical assessment and an ECG. Do not drive.

redFlags.label: Possible stroke
redFlags.message: Sudden facial drooping, arm weakness or difficulty speaking is a stroke until proven otherwise. Treatment works only within a few hours.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now and note the exact time symptoms began.

redFlags.label: Seizure
redFlags.message: A first seizure needs assessment to find the cause and to advise on driving and safety.
redFlags.action: Seek urgent assessment today. Call emergency services if the seizure lasted over five minutes or a second one followed.

redFlags.label: Significant gastrointestinal bleeding
redFlags.message: Vomiting blood, or passing black tarry stools, means bleeding inside the digestive tract.
redFlags.action: Go to an emergency department now.

redFlags.label: New jaundice
redFlags.message: Yellowing of the skin or eyes always needs blood tests to find out why.

redFlags.label: Sudden loss of vision
redFlags.message: Sight lost suddenly in one or both eyes needs assessment the same hour, whatever the cause.
redFlags.action: Go to an eye emergency department now.

redFlags.label: Thoughts of self-harm
redFlags.message: Thoughts of harming yourself or of being better off dead deserve help today. You do not have to be in crisis to reach out.
redFlags.action: Contact your doctor, a crisis line, or go to an emergency department now. If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services.

redFlags.label: New confusion coming on over hours or days
redFlags.message: Confusion that has come on over hours or days, or that comes and goes through the day, is delirium until proven otherwise. It is caused by something else -- an infection, a drug, pain, retention -- and that cause needs finding today.
redFlags.action: Seek same-day medical assessment. Take a list of all medications. Call emergency services if they are drowsy, feverish or cannot be roused properly.

disclaimer: This tool provides information about possible causes of symptoms. It is not a diagnosis and it cannot examine you. It does not replace assessment by a qualified clinician. If you feel very unwell, or your symptoms are getting rapidly worse, seek medical help immediately regardless of what this tool says.
